page.metaTitle: Price Monitoring Software — Automated Price Tracking | WebMonitor.fyi
page.metaDescription: Automated price monitoring across Amazon, Walmart, Target, eBay, and any other retailer. Set criteria in plain English, get alerts on drops, restocks, and changes.
page.h1: Price monitoring software for any website
page.subtitle: Track the product pages you care about most from one dashboard. Plain-English rules, email, Slack, and webhook alerts, checks as often as every 30 minutes.
page.intro: Price monitoring is the practice of tracking product pricing across the web for changes — drops, increases, promotional activations, restocks. WebMonitor.fyi handles the polling, change detection, and alerting so you don't have to refresh tabs. The price monitoring tool works with any publicly accessible product page: Amazon, Walmart, Target, Best Buy, eBay, Costco, hotel booking sites, electronics retailers, fashion sites, and direct-from-brand stores. Built for shoppers waiting on a deal, resellers tracking competitor pricing, procurement teams managing supplier catalogs, and travel planners watching hotel and flight rates.

features.title: Works on any retailer page
features.body: Not limited to a curated list — any publicly accessible product URL works: major retailers, direct-from-brand stores, and niche sites alike.

features.title: Plain-English criteria
features.body: Write the rule in normal language: "alert me when this drops below $X" or "tell me when a member-only price activates". No regex, no XPath, no scripting.

features.title: Adjustable check frequency
features.body: Checks as often as every 30 minutes (Pro) for limited-time deals and restock hunting. Hourly for everyday tracking. Daily for slow-moving items. Pick per monitor.

features.title: Multi-channel delivery
features.body: Email, Slack, or a generic JSON webhook into your own tooling. Match the channel to the urgency.

features.title: Check history
features.body: The dashboard keeps the last 50 checks per monitor, each with an AI summary — see when a price moved, when a listing changed, and what the monitor saw.

features.title: No alert spam
features.body: Smart deduplication: while the price and page state stay the same, the monitor stays quiet. You only hear about it when something actually changes.

steps.title: Add the product URL
steps.body: From the dashboard, click Add New Monitor and paste any product page link.

steps.title: Write the criterion
steps.body: Anything from "alert me on any change" to "notify me when this drops by 15% or more and is in stock for Prime shipping". The AI parses the natural-language criterion into a watch rule.

steps.title: Pick a frequency and a channel
steps.body: Intervals as short as 30 minutes (Pro) for limited-time deals; hourly or daily for general tracking. Email, Slack, or webhook.

steps.title: Get alerts when something changes
steps.body: The alert includes a plain-English summary of what changed and a link back to the listing.

page.limits: Price monitoring is constrained by what a retailer renders publicly. Personalized prices that only show after login, A/B-tested pricing that varies by user cookie, and prices hidden behind a member portal are outside what a public-page monitor can see. For those, an authenticated integration is required, which the standard product doesn't cover.

faq.a: Reading publicly available web pages is legal under US law and most other jurisdictions. WebMonitor uses standard web requests at reasonable intervals and does not bypass paywalls or login walls — if a page sits behind one, the monitor reports it rather than working around it. Anti-scraping case law (HiQ v. LinkedIn, etc.) has generally found public-page scraping permissible. We do not, however, provide legal advice — for high-volume commercial monitoring, check with counsel.

Aggressive sub-minute polling can trigger access limits on major retail sites. WebMonitor uses reasonable intervals (30 minutes is the fastest available) and conservative request handling so monitors stay practical for publicly available product pages.

faq.q: What's the difference between price monitoring and price comparison?
faq.a: Price comparison shows you the current price across multiple sites at one point in time (e.g., Google Shopping). Price monitoring tracks changes over time and alerts you when conditions are met. The two complement each other — compare once you have an alert.

faq.q: How is this different from browser extensions like Honey or CamelCamelCamel?
faq.a: Browser extensions are limited to specific retailers (CamelCamelCamel = Amazon only) and rely on you visiting the page. WebMonitor checks any retailer in the background at the interval you set — no browser tab required, no curation by the extension vendor.

The dashboard keeps the last 50 checks for every monitor, each with an AI summary — enough to see how a price has moved recently and whether the current price is genuinely a deal vs. a manufactured discount. For multi-year price archives, a dedicated history database like CamelCamelCamel complements it.
